sentences: One colossal mountain fills the picture and stands there, unmoving.
At its foot, tiny figures drive a train of mules along a path.
This is Travelers Among Mountains and Streams, painted by Fan Kuan in China's Northern Song dynasty.
It is a hanging scroll on silk more than two metres tall, painted in the early eleventh century, about a thousand years ago.
Today it belongs to the National Palace Museum in Taipei, and it is often called the highest peak of Chinese landscape painting.
Fan Kuan is said to have spent long periods living among the mountains, simply watching them.
According to old accounts, he decided that it was better to learn from nature itself than to copy the paintings of earlier masters.
Now look at the central peak.
A single, majestic mountain takes up most of the upper picture.
Its surface is covered with countless short, dabbed strokes, often compared to raindrops.
They make the rock feel dense, hard and immensely heavy.
In the foreground sit large boulders and trees.
The rocks in front, the wooded middle ground and the towering peak behind overlap one after another to build up depth.
Yet between the foreground and the mountain lies a band of empty, misty space, so you cannot quite tell how far away the great peak really is.
Look to the right of the summit.
A single thin waterfall drops from a great height, like a white thread.
Set against the vast dark rock, that slender line of water makes the mountain seem even taller and more dizzying.
In the lower right corner are the travellers of the title.
Men and pack mules loaded with goods make their way along the road.
They are so small that at first you may not notice them at all.
Each traveller shows how small we are before nature.
Above them, among the trees on a ridge, the roofs of a temple peek out.
Even the places where people live and pray sit quietly inside the landscape, almost hidden by it.
Hidden among the leaves in the lower right is the painter's own name.
In 1958 a scholar in Taiwan spotted this tiny signature, which had gone unnoticed for centuries.
The discovery strengthened the long tradition that the painting is by Fan Kuan himself.
The scroll is treated as one of the museum's greatest treasures.
To protect the fragile old silk, it is put on display only rarely, and only for a short time.
Step back and see it whole.
The mountain stands in silence, and the travellers pass beneath it on their way.
As you go about your own day, what great mountain might be standing quietly above your road?
